children: U.S. equity benchmarks observed a swift advancement after reports that Washington and Tehran are exploring a phased arrangement to restore commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
Reuters said negotiators are discussing a stepwise pact aimed at winding down hostilities, with markets treating even preliminary signals as a reduction in geopolitical risk.

Under the outline circulating among officials, Iran would reopen the waterway in return for the United States lifting its economic blockade and, potentially, granting access to frozen Iranian assets. The first phase would be designed to restore shipping while broader talks continue.

Sequencing remains the central obstacle though. Neither government wants to relinquish leverage first, leaving the talks fragile and any agreement contingent on simultaneous, verifiable steps rather than unilateral concessions.
Energy markets responded faster than stocks. Crude

that had been trading near $96.76 a barrel slid as futures fell to $93.62, reflecting expectations that a reopened strait could ease supply constraints. The quick drop underscored how tightly oil prices remain tied to prospects for unimpeded Gulf flows.

Investors will watch whether the discussions produce concrete sequencing language. Until both sides accept a balanced first step, the rebound in equities and the retreat in crude remain a reaction to possibility rather than a completed deal.

title: Hormuz reopening talks are back in play as Washington and Tehran discuss a phased deal
